assessment.strongestFinding: All fourteen roles now have explicit H0D01-H0D10 dependency slots, but current H24 exact opaque-ELF bindings remain zero; historical bytes and runtime hints cannot be promoted into that closure.
observed: H24 selected source contains thirteen composite entries, a property shim, a modem holder, and the helper itself before station policy.
H24 never reached this helper route live; its consumed D1 stopped at persistent HUD.
WSTA18 proves aggregate backend necessity but no individual role necessity.
The selected source path writes global SELinux policy load and best-effort enforce=0.
The selected source materializes native-global Binder rdevs 10:79, 10:80, and 10:81 and accepts both SD and historical cache whole-property roots.
inferred: Duplicated Binder context managers are likely to conflict, but actual runtime failure is unproved.
QRTR, PD, RFS, CNSS, and the current provider route are plausible dependencies but individually unproved.
cnss_diag is the first diagnostic ablation candidate but is not proved unrelated.
proposed: Use one generated duplicate-rejecting component manifest for construction, logs, health, cleanup, and evidence.
Run the same one-factor ablation and measurement contract before selecting either ownership topology.

Use the completed WP-H0-2 H0 design for corrected-baseline and exact-one-role planning; prove the public SD-free bootstrap superset and each row's static prerequisites before separately reviewed and authorized execution, then retire all ten H0D gates by their declared evidence classes before Option C implementation.

Apply the generated WP2-2 static policy to every future byte-derived surface declaration; the current H0 fixtures and sixteen negative cases retire no dependency gate and grant no execution eligibility.
Before execution qualification, derive the exact attended-session and ordinal budget from WP2-5b and obtain operator acceptance; the current one-to-one logical projection is thirty serial units.

Use the WP2-3 inventory to preserve selected-source facts, historical-only observations, and identity conflicts without claiming current H24 opaque ELF closure; use the generated WP2-4 schema only for future exact-run property observation and terminal validation, never as runtime proof.

invariants: H24 remains installed and its D1 remains consumed and unreplayable.
No successor inherits an SD path, global SELinux policy write, hidden duplicate, or hand-maintained process/order mismatch.
The proc capability-exposure incident is closed under either topology.
One ablation changes one variable and a failed unit is never the next baseline.
H24 is not the ablation baseline; the first complete corrected healthy variant becomes G0.
No future baseline reads the SD property snapshot or a copied private whole snapshot.
A private binderfs or property-service endpoint remains blocked until its exact H0D05 or H0D04 proof is bound; static shape acceptance is not execution proof.
Each corrected B0 placement binds the complete ordered fourteen-instance graph; later removals and integrations require explicit parent and transition lineage but remain non-executable.
Ablation results are generation- and order-conditioned; no global or terminal one-minimal set is claimed without a separate retest design.
Namespace membership is never proof that a global or shared kernel object is contained; QRTR, SELinux policy state, and ancestor proc magic links each require a named proved control.
WP2-4 retires neither H0D04 nor H0D10 and grants no D0 or live authority.
Historical artifact, linker, property, QMI, RFS, or identity evidence never fills a current H24 exact dependency slot unless a separately qualified current-generation consumer binds it.
Host fixtures do not substitute for future hardware necessity evidence.
Rollback, physical recovery, durable no-replay, target isolation, and final health remain mandatory.
nonGoals: Prove a Debian-supervised capsule feasible in this unit.
Declare any individual role required or unrelated without ablation.
Inspect private property or credential content.
Allocate an identity, mutate UFS, provision cache, or authorize a live action.

opportunities.title: Minimize the A90 vendor WLAN backend once for both ownership topologies
opportunities.summary: Correct the executable graph and global-policy hazards, then derive a finite component/property contract through one-factor ablation before topology selection.
desiredInvariants: One generated component manifest determines construction, order, health, cleanup, and evidence.
Every role has exact executable, identity, capability, FD, namespace, cgroup, readiness, and cleanup bindings.
Global SELinux policy/load/enforce writes are zero.
Property has exactly one proved terminal: absent or finite deterministic seed.
The same component/property contract serves reduced-native and Debian-capsule topology tests.
Remote workload code cannot name or control the privileged vendor backend.
opportunities.recommendation: Select topology-neutral ablation first and retain reduced native supervision as the reference boundary until the Debian capsule passes every explicit switch condition.

options.title: Rehost the H24 accumulated graph unchanged
options.summary: Move the current helper and its compatibility surfaces under another supervisor without reducing them.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It preserves the hidden duplicate and graph/order mismatch.
It preserves the global SELinux mutation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Preserves root services, global IPC, SD property assumptions, and global policy writes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Reject statically; do not qualify.

tradeoffs.assessment: Keeps a sixteen-process backend and recurring health writes before station policy.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No live benchmark because structural rejection precedes it.

tradeoffs.assessment: Retains all accumulated processes and compatibility state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use source count only as a rejection signal, not a measured RSS claim.

tradeoffs.assessment: Duplicate context managers may prevent readiness and H24 never exercised the route.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require duplicate rejection before any future run.

tradeoffs.assessment: Emitted order cannot identify the actual instance graph.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require generated instance manifest and exact receipts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Moves less code initially but carries every unresolved dependency forward.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rejected because short migration does not outweigh structural hazards.

residualRisks: No H24 live readiness proof exists.
Global security state can be changed.

implementationReadiness.rollback: H24 remains unchanged and no live action is authorized.

tradeoffs.assessment: Two PID 1 roles remain but the vendor graph may shrink materially.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It must preserve or relaunch the backend instead of removing it.
Remote workloads still require proc/fd/ns separation from the capsule.

tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove clean exec, private IPC, capability, proc/fd/ns, old-root, VMA, cgroup, and workload separation.

tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark the same component set against reduced native supervision.

tradeoffs.assessment: Could remove one administrative world only after real service reduction.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure steady-state RSS/PSS and process/thread/FD count.

options.title: Freeze a shared component and property contract first
options.summary: Correct the graph and define one-factor evidence and metrics before either supervisor topology becomes a candidate.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Graph generation and duplicate rejection close the 13/11 drift.
